title: Patterns in the booking system
idea: Incorporating design patterns means placing a known shape, like Strategy or Observer, exactly where a requirement varies or fans out.
points: Find the spots in the requirements that will change or grow.
Overlap rules differ per building, so `ConflictPolicy` becomes a Strategy.
Notify and audit react to a booking, so they become Observers.
`BookingService` depends only on the two interfaces, never on their implementations.

edges.caption: A request reaches the service. Its own steps never change.

edges.label: asks
edges.caption: The service asks the `ConflictPolicy` interface whether the slot clashes.

edges.label: implemented by
edges.caption: Today the rule is `BufferPolicy`. Swap it in `main` without editing the service.

edges.label: tells
edges.caption: After a save, the service tells every `BookingListener` it was given.
`AuditLogger` records the booking. A third listener needs no change to the service.

code.title: Strategy plus Observer
code.caption: The building wants a 15-minute gap between meetings. Only the policy knows that. Trimmed: a clash prints instead of throwing `RoomTakenException`, so the output shows the pattern at work.

walk.text: `main` picks the rule and the listeners; the service receives them through its constructor.
The Strategy interface: one question, answered by any rule.
`BufferPolicy` treats meetings closer than `gap` hours as a clash.
The Observer interface and two listeners that react to a booking.
The service passes only this room's bookings to the policy, then saves and tells each listener.

pitfalls: Do not add a pattern without a requirement that varies; it only adds indirection.
Keep listener work out of the booking rules; a failing email must not refuse a booking.
Inject the policy and listeners; a `new BufferPolicy()` inside the service locks the rule in.

quiz.q: What does the second `book` call print?
quiz.why: With a 0.25-hour gap, 11.0 is earlier than 11.0 + 0.25, so the slots clash. Doubles print as 11.0.

takeaway: Put a pattern where the requirements vary, and nowhere else.

starters: Would a Factory pattern help create the right ConflictPolicy per building?
Should listeners run synchronously or on a queue?
